Decision — monitord and Monitor

Status: accepted 2026-10-16.

The decision

  • monitord (services/monitord, kind service, layer core) runs once per host as its own unprivileged user. It samples the system and its processes, keeps recent history in memory and longer history in SQLite, and answers read verbs on the Bus. It runs headless; a mesh node with no desktop is a first-class host.
  • Monitor (apps/monitor, binary monitor, app id dev.mixos.monitor) is the egui task manager: processes, performance graphs, apps, services and users, in the shape people know from Windows Task Manager and GNOME Mission Center. It reads everything through monitord's verbs, never from /proc itself, so the same window shows any node on the mesh (monitord.<node>.bus).
  • monitord observes; it does not act. No verb signals, renices or stops anything.
    • The monitord command line acts locally as the person who runs it: monitord signal and monitord renice make the system call directly and the kernel decides, exactly like kill and renice.
    • Acting across users or across the mesh is hostd's job, as closed verbs behind grants (hostd decision), added one reviewed verb at a time.
  • A personality of the system binary. monitord's library exports main; cli/system carries it (one system binary). The unit runs /opt/mixos/bin/monitord serve.

History

TierResolutionKeptWhere
livethe sample interval (1 s)10 minutesmemory ring
short1 minute (avg, min, max)7 daysSQLite
long1 hour (avg, min, max)1 yearSQLite
  • SQLite (rusqlite, already in the system binary through the shell) holds only system-wide series: CPU, memory, swap, load, pressure, and one series per network interface and disk. Per-core and per-process series live in memory only; they are too many to keep.
  • The database is /var/lib/monitord/history.db, owned by monitord. It is a cache: deleting it loses history, nothing else.
  • Retention is configuration, so a small node can keep less.

Sampling

  • System-wide sampling runs all the time at 1 s. It reads a handful of /proc files and costs next to nothing.
  • The process table is sampled only while someone is reading it: a monitord.processes call holds the process sampler on for 30 s. An idle mesh node does not walk /proc every second. A cold call samples twice, a short interval apart, so CPU percentages are never zero by default.
  • monitord reads what an unprivileged user can read. A process's I/O counters and some of its details are readable only for monitord's own processes; elsewhere those fields are absent, never guessed. Wider reads are a later, reviewed capability (CAP_SYS_PTRACE or a hostd verb).

On the Bus

  • Read verbs (all queries): monitord.status, monitord.snapshot, monitord.processes, monitord.process, monitord.series and monitord.history. The verbs and their bodies are documented in the monitord manual.
  • A retained topic, monitord.summary, carries a small system summary every 5 s, so a dashboard of the whole mesh subscribes instead of polling.
  • The reply bodies are a public contract (contract = "public"), versioned in monitord's changelog. Monitor depends on the JSON, not on monitord's Rust types. If a second component needs those types, they are promoted to a library by review (AGENTS.md §2.2).

What it is built from

  • Phase 1 reads the kernel directly. /proc and /sys parsers are small, and each one reads from a root directory, so tests run against a fixture tree, the way hostd's do. No collection crate is needed yet.

  • Later phases use permissive crates, each checked against deny.toml when it enters:

    AreaCrate
    NVIDIAnvml-wrapper (MIT OR Apache-2.0)
    AMDlibamdgpu_top (MIT)
    Intel, and GPU use per process on every vendorqmlib (Apache-2.0)
    systemd units, login sessionszbus_systemd (MIT OR Apache-2.0)
    batterystarship-battery (ISC)
    graphs, tables (Monitor)egui_plot, egui_table (MIT OR Apache-2.0)

  • Code may be lifted from bottom (MIT) and systemd-manager-tui (MIT), with its notice kept (AGENTS.md §4).

  • GPL and other copyleft monitors are reference only: Mission Center and magpie, Resources, nvtop. Nobody copies or translates their code. Where one of them shows what to read, the reader is written fresh from the kernel's documentation.

Phases

  1. monitord: CPU, memory, swap, pressure, load, disks, network interfaces, the process table and tree; history; the Bus verbs and topic; the command line, with local signal and renice.
  2. Monitor: the egui window over phase 1, any node on the mesh.
  3. GPUs: NVIDIA, AMD and Intel, with use per process.
  4. systemd services and the Apps view (processes grouped by application).
  5. Sensors, fans, battery, power.
  6. Privileged readings (per-process network bytes over eBPF, SMART, RAPL energy, DMI) through a reviewed capability or hostd verbs.

Why

  • Every node on the mesh should be able to say what it is doing, in one shape, to any agent or window that asks, without ssh.
  • The split between a headless sampler and a window is already the right one in Mission Center (magpie and its GTK frontend), but that code is GPL-3.0 and MixOS is MIT OR Apache-2.0. Permissive Rust crates cover most of the same ground, and what they don't cover is small.
  • Keeping monitord read-only keeps it unprivileged, so it can run everywhere. Killing a process is already a kernel-checked system call for the local user; across users or nodes it is a privileged change, and those go through hostd.

Consequences

  • noded's built-in mon module (mon.status, mon.processes, mon.props.*) is superseded. Its verbs were never registered and nothing in the tree calls them. It is removed once monitord is installed on the mesh.
  • monitord adds a system user, monitord, and the state directory /var/lib/monitord.
  • Monitor's graphs and tables record their performance workloads (a 2,000-process table, a 64-core grid) before they are optimised (AGENTS.md §4.1).

Amendments

2026-10-16: Monitor's End task and Kill, and its widgets

  • Monitor acts on this node's processes the way the command line does. End task (SIGTERM) and Kill (SIGKILL) are local system calls made as the person running Monitor, and the kernel decides. They are off while another node is shown, and no Bus verb of monitord's is involved. Acting on another node, or as another user, stays hostd's.
  • Phase 2 adds no graph or table crate. The graphs are painted directly: a 64-core grid is 64 graphs a frame, which a plotting widget per graph would make heavy. The process table is egui_extras' TableBuilder, already in the tree. egui_plot and egui_table stay candidates for when a view needs what they add (zoom, axes, ragged rows).
